summary: Well‑executed, fully archived preregistered paired NetOps experiment that produced a degenerate ceiling outcome (200/200 SAFE) under shared‑generation semantics. The run and analysis are reproducible and well documented; the primary scientific inference is non‑informative for verifier efficacy and the manuscript appropriately reports that. Major remaining manuscript defects are presentation and citation form rather than execution or analysis errors.
critical_issues: Main narrative remains metadata‑heavy: long enumerations of artifact paths/SHAs and provenance bookkeeping are used in multiple sections, making the paper read like an artifact report rather than a focused conference paper; this impairs readability and discussion of scientific implications.

Related Work and other in‑text citations still appear as raw URLs/provenance fragments rather than conventional literature citations (author/year/venue) tied to the supplied verified bibliography; this reduces scholarly readability and makes it harder for readers to assess prior work.

Because of the presentation issues above, several claims and comparisons are presented with provenance fragments instead of concise, literature‑grounded statements—this must be corrected to meet normal conference prose expectations.
required_revisions: Compress and de‑emphasize detailed manifest/path/SHAs in the main text: replace long path lists with concise referential wording (e.g., “full execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the supplied bundle; representative identifiers appear in the Disclosure”) and move full manifest listings to the Disclosure or a compact appendix within the same five pages. (Resolvable from supplied artifacts.)

Replace all inline raw URLs/provenance fragments used as citations with conventional bibliographic citations (author, year, venue) drawn from the verified bibliography record; ensure every narrative citation is supported by an entry in the archived verified bibliography. (Resolvable from supplied artifacts.)

Rewrite one or two paragraphs (total ≤~200 words) to convert metadata‑heavy paragraphs into normal scholarly prose that: (a) summarizes provenance succinctly with a single archival pointer, (b) focuses discussion on scientific interpretation and implications rather than listing artifacts, and (c) preserves reproducibility by referring readers to the archived manifest for details. (Resolvable from supplied artifacts.)
optional_revisions: Shorten Related Work to the 3–5 closest methodological/empirical items and move peripheral citations to the references only to improve information density (can use the verified bibliography).

Add a very short table (≤1/2 page) that summarizes key resource trade‑offs (model_calls_used vs planned_model_calls; N tasks; generation semantics used) using numbers from execution_manifest.json to help operators; keep it compact to preserve page limit.

Add one concise sentence stating repair capability/status (e.g., “the guarded pipeline could invoke repairs but repair_provider_trace entries are null for confirmatory episodes, so no repairs were applied”) if not already crisply phrased in the Methods or Disclosure. (This can be produced from archived scoring JSONs.)
